nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Long summer days power the sedge meadows, willows and forest of the far north.

nodes.name: Peace-Athabasca Delta floods
nodes.desc: The inland delta of the Peace, Athabasca and Birch rivers; its water feeds the park's wetlands and meadows.

nodes.name: Wildfire
nodes.desc: Fire renews boreal forest and open meadow, resetting plant growth across the landscape.

nodes.name: Sedges
nodes.desc: Sedges form some of the large grass and sedge meadows UNESCO highlights in the park; they feed wood bison.

nodes.name: Bluejoint reedgrass
nodes.desc: A tall moist-ground grass recorded in the park area; a grazing food for bison.

nodes.name: Beaked willow
nodes.desc: A willow of wet ground. Wood bison eat willow leaves in summer, and beavers and moose browse willows.

nodes.name: White spruce
nodes.desc: A main conifer of the boreal forest, whose seeds feed red squirrels.

nodes.name: Dwarf red blackberry
nodes.desc: A low forest-floor berry plant recorded near the park; its fruit is eaten by bears and foxes.

nodes.name: Wood bison
nodes.desc: The park holds the world's largest wood bison herd. They graze grasses, sedges and forbs, and dig through snow for food.

nodes.name: Moose
nodes.desc: A large browser of willows and other woody plants, and a main prey of wolves and bears.

nodes.name: North American beaver
nodes.desc: Eats willow and sedges and builds dams; satellite images in 2007 revealed a dam about 850 m long in the park.

nodes.name: Meadow vole
nodes.desc: A small grass-eating rodent of meadows, eaten by foxes, bears and many other predators.

nodes.name: American red squirrel
nodes.desc: A forest squirrel that eats conifer seeds; lynx, foxes and wolves are recorded eating it.

nodes.name: Mallard
nodes.desc: A dabbling duck of the delta wetlands that eats plant matter and small aquatic animals.

nodes.name: Whooping crane
nodes.desc: The park is the main breeding area of this endangered crane, which nests on marshes and eats animals, tubers and berries.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: A scavenger and egg thief, recorded more than any other bird in the park area.

nodes.name: Red fox
nodes.desc: Hunts voles, squirrels, ducks and eats berries; it is also a predator of crane nests.

nodes.name: Canada lynx
nodes.desc: A forest cat that preys on red squirrels and beavers according to GloBI records.

nodes.name: American black bear
nodes.desc: An omnivore eating berries, grasses, voles and moose, and a recorded predator of crane nests.

nodes.name: Gray wolf
nodes.desc: UNESCO says the park is the only place where the wolf and wood bison predator-prey link has continued unbroken.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi and bacteria that break down dead plants and animals, returning nutrients to the wet soils.
